findings.title: Team access requires both admin and owner roles
findings.body: This condition grants the team path only when both checks return true. Team admins who are not owners—and owners not recognized as admins—are therefore denied access, even though the intent appears to allow either role. Use an OR between the checks.

findings.title: The server does not enforce unique guest addresses
findings.body: The input schema checks only email syntax, and this filter checks each value only against the attendees loaded before the request. Repeated addresses in the request, or case variants of an existing address, can all pass and be sent to createMany. This can create duplicate attendee records (or make the mutation fail if a database constraint rejects them); enforce uniqueness on normalized addresses server-side.

findings.title: Mixed-case addresses bypass the guest email blocklist
findings.body: Blocklist entries are lowercased, but the submitted guest address is compared without normalization. A mixed- or uppercase spelling of a blocked address therefore passes the filter and is added to the booking. Normalize the submitted address before checking the blocklist.

findings.title: Calendar updates use the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: This procedure allows an existing attendee to add guests, but it constructs EventManager with credentials for ctx.user. For an attendee caller, those are not the credentials for the organizer-owned calendar, so updating that calendar's attendee list can fail or be skipped. The attendee rows are already committed before this call, and a failure also prevents the email step, leaving guests persisted without the expected calendar update or notifications.

findings.title: Email classification uses requested guests rather than guests actually added
findings.body: The handler filters existing attendees out of uniqueGuests, but passes the original guests array to sendAddGuestsEmails. If a request contains both an existing attendee and a new address, the existing attendee is still classified as newly added and receives an AttendeeScheduledEmail, causing a duplicate booking confirmation or calendar invite. Pass uniqueGuests so notification types reflect the attendees actually inserted.

findings.title: The guest list has no size limit despite per-attendee fan-out
findings.body: This array is unbounded, and each accepted address creates an attendee row and adds work for calendar synchronization and email delivery. An authorized booking participant can submit thousands of unique addresses in one request, causing large database writes and a correspondingly large email fan-out. Enforce a reasonable maximum batch size (and consider rate limiting).
